additional_concerns: The circular preserves processing of pending pre-effective applications. It does not expressly establish that such an application permanently disqualifies the underlying change from substantive relief. The exclusion in candidates 1bf6918f, 4e6a162c, ce439b1c and ea4d1963 therefore remains an interpretation requiring confirmation.

Candidate 4d548f2e places legacy applications outside its question and scope; it does not determine their eligibility. Candidate b66b3e83 deliberately assesses substantive conditions only. Neither omission establishes a defect relative to its typed question.

The explicit commencement date supports the date comparison, but the circular does not specify a universal assessment-versus-implementation event test. Candidate 4e6a162c refers to proposed implementation in its question but compares an assessment date; those dates need not coincide.
The introductory home-supervision purpose does not expressly impose an additional item (ii) condition. Importing the distinct supervision condition from item (i) would add an unsupported restriction.

The two supplied missing dependency IDs have no identifying metadata linking either to a particular external authority. No catalogue mapping can be inferred. Relevant FAQs, transition guidance and applicable home-jurisdiction requirements are absent.

The substantive predicates correctly test possible local policy implications and any novel or complex feature of the whole selected change. Their legal classifications remain supplied inputs, not determinations made by the formulas.
Removal of prior approval does not establish overall compliance or eliminate notification, filing or post-vetting requirements. The candidates generally preserve this distinction.
